title: Build together: the Today page
goal: Take the first piece of the command center through the six steps: design, prompt, review, test, ship, log. You leave with a project folder, a rules file for your AI, and a Today page that opens with a double-click.
you_need: The Claude app or Claude Code

steps.do: Design: Double-click Launch in the starter folder, then press Start the six steps.
steps.see: The home screen with eight pieces that say Not built yet, then the build page for week 1.
steps.tip: This folder is your project folder. Keep it somewhere you will find it, such as Documents.

steps.do: Design: Under step 1, open The rules file for the AI and read the rules out loud.
steps.see: It drafts and a person sends. It says what it is unsure about. It never invents a number. It never sends, pays, posts or deletes.
steps.tip: The same rules sit in your folder as CLAUDE.md. Add one rule of your own there after class.

steps.do: Design: Read the design note: who uses it, the one question it answers, what is on it, what done means.
steps.see: Four short answers. The question is: what needs me today?
steps.tip: Design comes before the prompt. If you cannot answer the four questions, the AI cannot either.

steps.do: Prompt: Press Copy the build prompt, paste it into the Claude app or Claude Code, and send. Save the file it makes as week-1-today.js in the pieces folder, and say yes to replace.
steps.see: Your computer asks whether to replace week-1-today.js. That question means the name is right.
steps.tip: In the Claude app you save the file yourself. In Claude Code it writes the file for you.

steps.do: Review: Press I saved the file. Look again. Then read the Today page against the design note and find the one thing it got wrong.
steps.see: The Today page, with the one thing first at the top and Jordan's list under it.
steps.tip: Do not ask whether it is right. Ask which one thing is wrong.

steps.do: Test: Press How it was built, go to step 4, and run the three checks with the sample business. Tick each one you saw.
steps.see: Three ticks, and the words Three checks passed.
steps.tip: The checks were written before the build. That is what makes them a test.

steps.do: Ship: In step 5, type your runbook line: the step, the sign it worked, how to undo it.
steps.see: Three short answers, saved as you type.
steps.tip: For example: each morning I write today's list. The first thing is at the top. Start over puts it back.

steps.do: Log: In step 6, type what changed and why, then press Add to my change log.
steps.see: The line under the button says your change log has 1 line.
steps.tip: Next Wednesday we build the board, and the page that shows this log.

real_life: Tomorrow morning: press My business on the home screen, open Today, and write your own list. The first line is the one thing first.
Open CLAUDE.md in your project folder and add one rule that is true only for your business.
Write down three things you retype every week. Those are the next pieces worth building.
if_it_breaks: The AI is slow, or the page does not show after you saved the file: take the finished week-1-today.js from the pieces folder of the complete project, save it in your pieces folder, and keep going. The lesson is the six steps, not the typing.
Your computer did not ask to replace the file: the name is not exactly week-1-today.js, or it is not in the pieces folder. Rename it, move it, and press Look again.
The page says the file needs a fix: copy that sentence to the AI and ask for the whole file again. Start over with the sample data puts the Today page back.
